selector.champion: Mirror-image dextrocardia with acute inferior wall and right ventricular myocardial infarction due to proximal right coronary artery occlusion
selector.rationale: The patient's presentation of chest pain, vomiting, and elevated serum troponin I level, combined with ECG findings of ST-segment elevations and QRS complexes indicating right ventricular activation, support the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction. The presence of dextrocardia with the right atrium and ventricle on the left side and the left atrium and ventricle on the right side, as seen on the transthoracic echocardiogram, and the total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery on coronary angiography, make the champion diagnosis the most specific and evidence-supported choice.

rejected.label: Dextrocardia with Situs Inversus
rejected.why: While the patient has dextrocardia, the diagnosis does not fully explain the acute presentation of chest pain and elevated troponin levels.

rejected.label: Cor pulmonale
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of pulmonary hypertension or right ventricular hypertrophy due to pulmonary disease, making this diagnosis less likely.
